interpretation_notes: Each boundary marker separates two proposed word-like or meaningful units.
Read a marked string such as Donne¦-¦le¦-¦moi as the proposed units Donne, -, le, -, moi.
Spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, and punctuation can be separate units; do not reject an example merely because these separators have been split out.
Deterministic validation has already checked that removing the boundary markers recreates the input exactly.

usually acceptable here: verb, hyphens, and clitic pronouns are visible meaningful/separator units

candidate.rationale: A proper noun compound word showing that named entities need careful segmentation despite hyphenation.

review.strongest_reason: Unhelpful split of fixed proper name
review.explanation: Champs-Élysées is a conventional proper noun. Splitting it as Champs, -, Élysées implies productive, recombinable parts, but especially "Élysées" is not a free, learner-reusable element. Per the guidance on named entities, keep the conventional form intact unless a clear pedagogical gain exists; here the hyphen split adds no value.
notes: For demonstrating transparent hyphenated compounds, prefer items like porte¦-¦monnaie or arc¦-¦en¦-¦ciel.
If contextually included (les Champs-Élysées), the article could be a separate unit, but the name itself should remain intact.
